solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Making appearance, friend is boxing boxer in ring

parts.note: a mate is a friend

indicators.note: in means the boxed-up group sits inside the word ring

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: boxing means the word is closes around the boxer, as a box encloses its contents

parts.note: Muhammad Ali, the famous heavyweight boxer

explanation.surface: A friend turns up at a boxing match with a boxer in the ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boxing' and 'in' both nest one piece inside another; 'ring' looks like the boxing venue but is taken as written.
explanation.definitionFit: Materialising means coming into view, so it is a synonym of making an appearance.

clue.text: Mother with dry chop for boy

parts.note: ma is a familiar word for mother
TT stands for teetotal, someone who stays dry
to hew is to chop

explanation.surface: A mother, off the drink, chops something up for her son.
explanation.walkthrough: TT, short for teetotal, is the crossword's usual 'dry'.
explanation.definitionFit: Matthew is a boy's given name, so it is an example of a boy.

clue.text: Hammer Thor's held making entry

indicators.note: to hammer something is to beat it out of shape, so these letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: The god Thor grips his hammer as he makes his entrance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hammer' looks like Thor's famous weapon but is the anagram signal for THORSHELD.
explanation.definitionFit: A threshold is the sill of a doorway, the point of entry to a building.

clue.text: Cash examined with naked eye

parts.note: to read something is to examine it

indicators.note: naked means the word eye is stripped of its outer letters

explanation.surface: Banknotes are checked by eye, without a magnifier.
explanation.walkthrough: READY is British slang for cash, as in 'the ready' or 'ready money'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ready money is cash in hand, and the ready on its own is slang for money.

clue.text: Named idiot regularly ringing journalist

parts.note: an ass is a fool or idiot

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of the word ringing

parts.note: ED, short for editor, is the usual crossword journalist

explanation.surface: A fool is named for repeatedly phoning a reporter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly ringing' looks like making phone calls; it picks the even letters of RINGING to give IGN.
explanation.definitionFit: To be assigned to a post is to be named or appointed to it.

clue.text: Harm creature of folklore, fairy getting wings removed

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous sprite of folklore

indicators.note: the wings are the outer letters of the word fairy, so they are cut off

explanation.surface: A folklore imp harms a fairy by tearing off its wings.
explanation.walkthrough: FAIRY loses its outer letters, its 'wings', to give AIR.
explanation.definitionFit: To impair something is to damage or weaken it, a synonym of harm.

clue.text: Nasty lump is on this writer's rash

indicators.note: on means the setter's I've is placed after the rearranged letters
nasty suggests something ugly and misshapen, so these letters are put into a new order

parts.note: this writer is the setter, I, and 'this writer's' reads as I've, I have

explanation.surface: The setter complains of a nasty lump and an itchy rash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nasty' rearranges LUMPIS into IMPULS; 'rash' looks like a skin complaint but is an adjective here.
explanation.definitionFit: A rash act is hasty and unconsidered, which is the sense of impulsive.

clue.text: Despondency of Grand Master drawing in game

indicators.note: drawing in means the chess title's letters pull the game inside them

parts.note: GM is the abbreviation for the chess title Grandmaster
loo is an old card game

explanation.surface: A chess grandmaster is downcast after drawing a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drawing' suggests a drawn chess game but means pulling in. LOO is a card game once popular in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Gloom is a mood of sadness and low spirits, a synonym of despondency.

clue.text: Hard king stuck-up, shaking head

parts.note: K is the abbreviation for king, as in chess

indicators.note: shaking head means the first letter of the word for stuck-up is shaken off

parts.note: snotty means snobbish or stuck-up

explanation.surface: A stern, snobbish king shakes his head in disapproval.
explanation.walkthrough: SNOTTY loses its first letter to give NOTTY.
explanation.definitionFit: A knotty problem is a hard, intricate one, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Headwear goes over graduate

indicators.note: over means the word for goes is placed over and around the graduate

parts.note: goes, as in 'your go', means turns
a BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate

explanation.surface: Mortarboard hats go on the graduate's head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes' is the noun, as in taking turns, not the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Turbans are wound cloth head coverings, so they are a kind of headwear.

clue.text: Fare that's substance of dad jokes?

parts.note: pop is a familiar word for dad
corn is stale, corny humour

explanation.surface: The stuff of groan-worthy dad jokes is the subject.
explanation.walkthrough: Dad jokes are proverbially corny, so the whole clue also reads as a description of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Popcorn is a snack, an item of food, and fare means food served.

clue.text: Reportedly, fish important for dog

indicators.note: reportedly means the clue words are heard as they sound, not as they are written

parts.note: huss is a fish, a kind of dogfish, and key means important; huss key

explanation.surface: A report claims a fish matters a great deal to a dog.
explanation.walkthrough: HUSS is a British fishmonger's name for dogfish, and KEY means important.
explanation.definitionFit: The husky is a breed of sled dog, so it is an example of a dog.

clue.text: Bird from lake caught by cunning cat turning

indicators.note: caught by means the lake's letter is held inside the word for cunning

parts.note: guile is cunning or craftiness
L is the map abbreviation for lake

indicators.note: turning means the male cat is read backwards

parts.note: a tom is a male cat

explanation.surface: A wily cat turns tail after catching a bird by the lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' reverses TOM to give MOT.
explanation.definitionFit: The guillemot is a black-and-white seabird of the auk family.

clue.text: Bad news, doom for fellers, perhaps

indicators.note: bad suggests something gone wrong, so these letters are spoiled into a new order

explanation.surface: Grim news spells doom for those men.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fellers' looks like slang for men but means people who fell trees; 'perhaps' marks an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Woodsmen work in forests and fell trees, so they are examples of tree fellers.

clue.text: Enigmatic south-eastern island hiding activity at centre

indicators.note: hiding means the Greek island keeps the central letters inside it

parts.note: Crete is a Greek island

indicators.note: at centre means taking the middle letters of the word activity

explanation.surface: Something mysterious is going on at the heart of a south-eastern island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at centre' takes the middle two letters of an eight-letter word, and 'hiding' puts them inside the island.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone secretive keeps things hidden and is hard to read, which is the sense of enigmatic.

clue.text: Somewhat civil, if you knock

indicators.note: Somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A polite request: be somewhat civil if you knock at the door.
explanation.definitionFit: To knock someone is to criticise or disparage them, and to vilify is to abuse them verbally.

clue.text: Put in grave challenge with appraisal

parts.note: to inter is to bury, to put in a grave
to vie is to compete or challenge

explanation.surface: A grave challenge is put in alongside an appraisal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grave' looks like an adjective meaning serious, but it is the burial place.
explanation.definitionFit: An interview is an assessment of a candidate, a form of appraisal.

clue.text: Sink a gin, drunk with lush

indicators.note: drunk suggests something reeling and disordered, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A drunkard knocks back a gin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sink a gin' reads as drinking; 'Sink' is the definition and 'lush' is part of the anagram, not the drinker.
explanation.definitionFit: To languish is to decline or waste away, so it means to sink in health or spirits.

clue.text: Bishop spotted cubes on old garment

indicators.note: on means the cubes are placed after the abbreviation for old

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
dice are cubes marked with spots

explanation.surface: A bishop spots some dice on an old piece of clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spotted' reads as noticed, but it describes the dots on dice.
explanation.definitionFit: A bodice is the close-fitting upper part of a woman's dress, an item of clothing.

clue.text: Purchase German booze we're told to divide

indicators.note: we're told means the words are heard spoken rather than read

parts.note: to purchase is to buy, and Sekt is German sparkling wine; buy Sekt

explanation.surface: Someone is told to buy German booze and split it.
explanation.walkthrough: SEKT is German sparkling wine.
explanation.definitionFit: To bisect is to cut into two equal parts, a specific way to divide.

clue.text: Ace fast stuffing cuddly toy to be gifted

indicators.note: stuffing means the ace and the fast are packed inside the toy, like filling

parts.note: a ted is a teddy bear, a cuddly toy
A is the abbreviation for ace in cards
Lent is the Christian season of fasting

explanation.surface: Fast work stuffing a teddy bear makes for a gifted toymaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fast' reads as quick but is the Lenten fast; 'stuffing' fits the teddy bear picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Talented and gifted both describe someone with natural ability.

clue.text: Indecisive replacing article in journal with another

indicators.note: replacing means one article in the journal is swapped for a different one

parts.note: a diary is a daily journal
a is the indefinite article
another article here is the definite article, the

explanation.surface: A dithering writer keeps swapping articles in a journal.
explanation.walkthrough: In DIARY the indefinite article A is replaced by the definite article THE.
explanation.definitionFit: Dithery describes someone who dithers, wavering and unable to make a decision.

clue.text: Upset and sad I'm terribly unknown

indicators.note: terribly suggests something badly done, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: Y is one of the algebraic letters for an unknown quantity

explanation.surface: Someone upset and sad confesses they are terribly anonymous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terribly' rearranges SADIM into DISMA.
explanation.definitionFit: Dismay is distress or consternation, and as a verb it means to upset someone.

clue.text: Distress as criminal fires gun outside loudly

indicators.note: outside means the shuffled letters sit around the musical letter for loudly
criminal suggests something crooked or wrong, so these letters are bent into a new order

parts.note: F, forte, is the musical direction for loudly

explanation.surface: A criminal fires a gun in the street, causing distress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminal' shuffles FIRESGUN into SUFERING, and 'outside' puts it around F.
explanation.definitionFit: Suffering is pain or misery, a synonym of distress.

clue.text: Enclose space in fine church

indicators.note: in means the printing space goes inside the letters for fine and church

parts.note: F is the pencil-grading abbreviation for fine
CE stands for Church of England
an en is a printing space, half an em

explanation.surface: A churchyard space is enclosed with fine railings.
explanation.walkthrough: An EN is a printer's space.
explanation.definitionFit: To fence land is to surround it with a barrier, which is to enclose it.

clue.text: Tile is about splitting risk

indicators.note: splitting means the word for about breaks the word for risk into two parts

parts.note: a bet is a risk or wager
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A roofer warns that tile splitting is a risk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tile' is old slang for a hat, not a roof tile.
explanation.definitionFit: Tile is old slang for a hat, and a beret is a soft round cap.

clue.text: Crude language

definitions.meaning: the early programming language for beginners

explanation.definitionFit: Basic means elementary or crude, and BASIC is a simple computer programming language.

clue.text: Fix fiddle with timber beginning to mould

parts.note: a con is a fiddle or swindle
fir is a softwood timber

indicators.note: beginning to means taking the first letter of the word mould

explanation.surface: A carpenter fiddles with timber that is starting to go mouldy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fix' reads as repair, but it means to settle or make certain.
explanation.definitionFit: To confirm arrangements is to make them definite, which is to fix them.

clue.text: Enthuse one gutted niece holding tears back

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: holding means the outside letters of niece hold the reversed tears between them
gutted means the word niece loses its insides, leaving only the outer letters
back means the word for tears is read backwards

parts.note: rips are tears, as in torn cloth

explanation.surface: A gutted niece holds back her tears, needing someone to lift her spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tears' reads as crying, but it means rips; 'gutted' fits the surface's upset niece yet only empties the word.
explanation.definitionFit: To inspire someone is to fill them with enthusiasm, so it means to enthuse them.

clue.text: Reach view why turbulent year's all over for Trump

indicators.note: turbulent means stormy and disordered, so these letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: Y is the abbreviation for year; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: A political commentator says the year's chaos means it is all over for Trump.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turbulent' rearranges REACHVIEWWHY. 'for Trump' points to an American idiom rather than an election result.
explanation.definitionFit: Every which way is an American phrase meaning in all directions, scattered all over the place.
